hook: A 194-page section of the FBI's long-running 62-HQ-83894 flying disc case file, spanning June 1947 to July 1968, but text extraction via pymupdf yielded no readable content — the pages are almost certainly scanned photographic images rather than digitized text, with only a single declassification stamp recoverable: 'Authority: DECLASSIFIED NND 90986'.
why_it_matters: This section is notable primarily for what the official description claims it contains rather than what could be extracted: Oak Ridge, TN photographic evidence (a sensitive nuclear site), technical proposals on potential UAP propulsion systems, and eyewitness testimonies spanning the entire early UFO era. The fact that the FBI maintained a two-decade active case file — and that this release includes pages not on the FBI Vault with fewer redactions — makes it a potentially significant primary source, if the images can be OCR'd or reviewed manually.
key_findings: Text extraction produced no readable document content across all 194 pages; the only recoverable text is the declassification authority stamp 'NND 90986', indicating the document was processed through the National Declassification Center.

Per official description, the case file includes photographic evidence from Oak Ridge, TN — a highly sensitive Atomic Energy Commission nuclear facility — suggesting the FBI was tracking UAP incidents near nuclear infrastructure.
The case file's date range (June 1947–July 1968) covers the full arc of the classic UFO era, from the Kenneth Arnold sighting through the height of Project Blue Book.

Official description notes this release contains 'several newly declassified pages' and 'only minor redactions' compared to the FBI Vault version, implying substantive new content not previously public.
The document includes a single page with redaction markers (per metadata: 1 page, 0.0% blacked-out area), suggesting redactions are minimal or symbolic rather than substantive.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The case file spans 1947–1968, the exact operational period of Project Blue Book, and FBI flying disc case files were coordinated with Air Force intelligence during this era.
Official description explicitly cites photographic evidence from Oak Ridge, TN, which was a core Atomic Energy Commission facility, placing UAP activity at a nuclear site.
FBI UFO case files from this period were routinely shared with Air Force intelligence at Wright-Patterson, which hosted Project Blue Book and maintained the official military UAP investigation.
Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is explicitly named in connection with photographic evidence in this file, directly linking the document to DOE/AEC nuclear laboratory UAP incidents.
